column1: # Akkadian for the "Write in ..." tool (scribe.js); built by scripts/make-scribe.ps1. Generated by make-cuneiform.ps1.
# The keys: the syllables of the Old Babylonian script (Borger's values, _cuneiform-values.tsv, which also lets any other
# value be typed), common word signs (typed in capitals, as Assyriologists write them) and determinatives ({d}).
# engine=syllabic: syllables joined by hyphens, or a whole word split into the fewest signs of the keys (šarrum: šar-ru-um).

column4: Akkadian, the language of Babylon and Assyria, was written in cuneiform, taken over from the Sumerians: signs pressed into clay with a reed, standing for syllables or for whole words.

column2: The cuneiform of Babylonia in the age of Hammurabi (about 1800–1600 BCE), the script of law, letters and literature across the Near East; the last dated tablet was written in 75 CE.

Type syllables joined by hyphens, as Assyriologists do (a-wi-lum), or a whole word, which is split into signs for you (šarrum → šar-ru-um). Type sh, s. and t. for š ṣ ṭ, and h for ḫ. Word signs in capitals (LUGAL, KUR); a determinative in braces ({d}AMAR.UTU, Marduk). Any value with an index works too: u2 or ú.
